title: Notification classes and relationships
idea: The class design splits a notification into who receives it, what it says, which channel carries it, and which provider delivers it, each in its own type.

analogy.text: A post office. The form letter is the template, the address book is the recipient, and couriers are providers.
analogy.breaks: A post office picks one courier; we fail over to another.

points: `Notification` owns its id, idempotency key, rendered message and status.
`Recipient` maps each `Channel` to an address, which may be missing.
`Template` belongs to one channel and fails loudly on a missing value.
`Provider` is an interface; each vendor is one class behind it.

edges.label: creates
edges.caption: The service creates one Notification per accepted request and keeps it by id and key.

edges.label: uses 1
edges.caption: Each Notification is built for one Recipient. It keeps only the resolved address, inside its Message.

edges.label: uses 1
edges.caption: It is rendered from one Template. Rendering happens once, at creation.

edges.label: has-a 1
edges.caption: The rendered result is an immutable Message: address, subject and body.

edges.label: has-a 1
edges.caption: A Template belongs to one Channel, so an SMS template never goes out as email.

edges.label: uses 1..* per channel
edges.caption: The service holds an ordered list of Providers per Channel. Order means failover order.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: Each vendor is a class that implements Provider. The service never sees vendor details.

edges.label: sends
edges.caption: A Provider only gets the Message. It knows nothing about templates or users.

code.title: The domain model
code.caption: Records for values, one class with state, and the provider interface. The service arrives on the next page.

walk.text: Ana has email and phone but no device token. Build an OTP notification.
Print the address, the rendered body, the missing push address, and the SENT state.
Leaving out the code value makes construction fail, so no half-filled message exists.
`Recipient.address` returns an Optional: a channel address may not exist.
`Template.fill` replaces each name in braces and throws on a missing value.
`Provider` is the swap point: one method that sends a Message.
The constructor resolves the address and renders once; `markSent` allows only PENDING to SENT.

pitfalls: Do not render templates inside the provider; render once so retries send identical text.
Never silently send an empty value when a template parameter is missing.
Do not make channel subclasses of Notification; channel is data, delivery is the provider.

quiz.q: What is the last line ClassModel prints?
options: body: Hi Ana, your code is
quiz.why: Ana has a phone, so the address resolves. The params hold `name` but not `code`, so `fill` throws with "missing code".

takeaway: Recipient, Template, Message and Provider each own one reason to change.
